decisions.justification: Q1 asked whether to skip, generate an alternative, or abort, and the user chose abort with no overwrite or skipping.
Q5 and Q6 asked about runtime rollback and the attainable atomicity contract, and the user chose best-effort transactional rollback.
Q9 addressed only exact same-name mappings, not whether files already matching the target naming scheme belong in the rename set.
The agent never specifically asked how to handle a target occupied by a source that would itself move later in the same run.
The agent never asked or settled what a second identical run should do.
The agent never asked or settled the semantics of case-only renames on case-insensitive filesystems.
Q3, Q4, and Q7 asked about clash details, aborted-run output, exit status, runtime errors, and rollback-failure reporting.
Q4 and Q8 asked whether plans should be printed before execution or only completed renames after full success, and the user chose the latter.

mustPreserveKept: user-facing output on stdout and diagnostics on stderr

notes: The session thoroughly settled collision handling, practical rollback, and failure diagnostics, and those choices are visible in the implementation. It nevertheless missed self-inclusion, transient collisions, repeat-run behavior, and case-only filesystem behavior; the implementation also cannot strictly guarantee either acceptance goal because rollback can fail and the existence-check/rename sequence has an overwrite race on filesystems where rename replaces an existing target.
